purpose: Pimavanserin is used to treat hallucinations and delusions that can happen in people with Parkinson's disease psychosis. These are experiences where a person sees, hears, or strongly believes things that are not real. It helps reduce these disturbing symptoms so daily life feels more manageable.
how_it_works: This medicine works by blocking certain receptors in the brain called serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. Think of these receptors like locks — pimavanserin acts like a key that blocks the lock so that too much serotonin activity does not cause false perceptions. Unlike older antipsychotics, it does not strongly block dopamine, which is important because blocking dopamine can make Parkinson's movement symptoms worse.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include swelling in your legs or feet, nausea, confusion, and constipation. Some people may also feel unusually tired or have trouble walking. These side effects are usually mild but tell your doctor if they bother you.
warnings: Important: This medication carries a serious warning — older adults with dementia-related psychosis who take antipsychotics like this one have a higher risk of death, so it should only be used for Parkinson's disease psychosis. It can also affect the heart's electrical rhythm (called QT prolongation), so tell your doctor about all your medications and heart conditions. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 34 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Some people may start at a lower dose of 10 mg once daily if they are taking certain other medications that interact with it. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep a steady level in your body.
